problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨2{u}^{3},\,u{v}^{2},\,2v⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=3.$

feedback.problem: Find the equation of the tangent plane to the surface generated by the vector-valued function $r(u,v)=⟨{u}^{2}-{v}^{2},\,u+v,\,uv⟩$ at the point where $u=1$ and $v=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We first compute the tangent vectors to the grid curves:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂u},\,\frac{∂y}{∂u},\,\frac{∂z}{∂u}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂u}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂u}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨2u,\,1,\,v⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(u,v) & =⟨\frac{∂x}{∂v},\,\frac{∂y}{∂v},\,\frac{∂z}{∂v}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂v}({u}^{2}-{v}^{2}),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(u+v),\,\frac{∂}{∂v}(uv)⟩ \\  & =⟨-2v,\,1,\,u⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate these vectors when $u=1$ and $v=1$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}_{u}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,1,\,1⟩ \\ {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) & =⟨-2(1),\,1,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-2,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, a normal vector to the surface is

$$
\begin{aligned}n & ={r}_{u}^{′}(1,1)\times {r}_{v}^{′}(1,1) \\  & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & 1 \\ -2 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =⟨|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,-|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Since the parameters $u=1$ and $v=1$ correspond to the point 

$$
({1}^{2}-{1}^{2},\,1+1,\,1\cdot 1)=(0,2,1),
$$

the equation of the tangent plane is

$$
\begin{aligned}n\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨0,\,-4,\,4⟩\cdot ⟨x,\,y-2,\,z-1⟩ & =0 \\ 0\cdot x+(-4)\cdot (y-2)+4\cdot (z-1) & =0 \\ -4y+4z+4 & =0 \\ -y+z+1 & =0 \\ y-z & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
